label: first m/t/w input in the original phase, or <DEL> when the sequence starts with d/b/f/h/3/y/c/q/u/k
explanation: Input-driven token detector with two parts. (1) Original phase: fires when the input is m or t (about 33% rate, roughly 47% of activation mass) or w (15% rate, weaker), mostly on their first occurrence (in_first=1 holds 93% of mass), and less often on the last one or two original positions. (2) Delimiter step: fires on <DEL> (24% rate, 42% of mass), which includes many of the strongest activations (max at <DEL>). Here firing depends on the first original token, the one about to be output: much more likely when orig(0) is in d/b/f/h/3/y/c/q/u/k, and more likely for short L. It is nearly silent in the copy phase (1% rate, 5% of mass, mostly a weak tail at recall_idx 1). It does not fire on most other letters or digits. The predicate gets dev F1 0.60 and mass recall 0.82. Precision is the limit: only about 56% of m/t inputs fire, and no clear positional or contextual rule I tested recovers the rest.
